meta.title: BoxBox · Who wins on Sunday?
meta.description: Win and podium chances for the next F1 race from the starting grid, the circuit and the race-day forecast. An XGBoost model trained on real results since 2022 and refit after every Grand Prix.

header.theme: Switch between light and dark mode

intro.title: Who wins on Sunday?
intro.lede: Pick an upcoming Grand Prix and set the grid. The weather comes from the forecast for race start, and the model works out every driver's chance of winning and of reaching the podium.

setup.title: The race
setup.forecast: Open-Meteo forecast for the first two hours from lights out · {start}
setup.noForecast: No forecast yet: it arrives on {date}. Until then the model runs without weather and assumes a dry track.
setup.noRaces: No races left on the calendar. The grid opens again when the next season's schedule is out.

grid.title: Starting grid
grid.hint: Drag a driver to another slot, or tap two drivers to swap them.
grid.resetHint: Back to the starting order of the last race
grid.selected: Selected. Tap another driver to swap.

predict.stale: You changed the setup. Predict again to update.

board.title: Pit board
board.empty: Set up the race and press “Predict race”. The most likely podium shows up here.
board.limit: Heads-up: in the backtest the model's favourite won {model} of races, while “pole sitter wins” was right {baseline} of the time.

table.title: Predicted order
table.caption: Normalised over all 22 drivers: win chances add up to 100 % and podium chances to 300 %.

review.title: Race by race
review.intro: Before each {season} Grand Prix the model only knew the earlier races. Afterwards it learns the result and is refit.
review.won: {driver} won, from P{grid}: we gave them {p}.
review.tally: {season}: the model's favourite won {hits} of {races} races; the pole sitter, {pole}.
review.label: {season} · Rd {round}

trust.title: How far to trust it
trust.intro: Walk-forward backtest: the model predicted {races} races from the last 3 seasons without having seen them, and was compared with a simple rule that only uses the grid.
trust.honest: The model ranks the whole field better (AUC and log loss), but when it has to name a single winner it is right less often than “pole sitter wins”. Read it as chances, not a sure bet.
trust.footer: Data to {dataTo} · {model} {version} · Results from Jolpica, weather from Open-Meteo. Independent project, not affiliated with Formula 1.

errors.offlineTitle: No signal from the pit wall

history.title: How good is it?
history.lede: Before every Grand Prix of the last three seasons the model was trained only on the earlier races and predicted the whole grid. Here is each prediction next to what actually happened.
history.caption: Predicted order by win chance (normalised over the grid), with the real finishing position on the right.
history.winnerRankHint: Where the eventual winner sat in our list on average (1 = our favourite).
history.allHint: Tap a race to see its full prediction.
